narrative.overview: A check reads as a short, calm column of white cards on a soft sage ground. Each card answers one question in plain words: what you asked, what the research says, the sentences themselves, what was searched, what wasn't. The interface is friendly and familiar so the evidence can be the interesting part.
keyCharacteristics: A single 720px column on every screen; no sidebars.
Soft-cornered white cards with one gentle shadow.
One orange, and it only ever marks something you can press.
Our voice is a rounded humanist sans; the literature's voice is an italic serif.
Verdict colours are inks for words and marks, never fills that shout.

rules.name: The Pressable Orange Rule
rules.body: If it is orange, it can be pressed; if it can be pressed, its primary state is orange. Never use orange for a verdict, a status or decoration.

rules.name: The Calm Verdict Rule
rules.body: A verdict is a coloured word and a mark on a flat bar, never a coloured badge, gauge or ring.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The serif is the literature talking. Never set our own copy in it.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Scores, counts, dates, PMIDs and times use tabular lining figures (.num).

dos: Do give each card one question and a heading that names it.
Do put limits (what was searched, skipped and dropped) in the same stack as the verdict.
Do keep the not-medical-advice card directly after the verdict.
donts: Don't use orange for anything that can't be pressed.
Don't show the score as a ring, gauge or big hero number.
Don't nest cards inside cards; inner groups are tiles or quote blocks.
Don't set our own copy in the serif, or quotes in the sans.
Don't load fonts or scripts from another host; the content security policy forbids it.
